intro.author: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, a priest from Anathoth (1:1). His scribe Baruch wrote down many of his messages as he dictated them (36:4, 32). Chapter 52 is a historical appendix (see 51:64).
intro.written: Jeremiah prophesied from about 627 BC (1:2) until after Jerusalem fell in 586 BC, finally in Egypt (chapters 43–44). The book was likely compiled during the exile.
intro.audience: Judah and Jerusalem in their last decades, the exiles in Babylon (chapter 29), and the refugees in Egypt
intro.setting: Jeremiah lived through Judah's final forty years: Josiah's reform, Assyria's collapse, Egypt's brief control, and Babylon's rise under Nebuchadnezzar. He warned that Babylon would conquer Jerusalem and urged surrender, which made him seem a traitor; he was beaten, jailed and thrown into a cistern. The ancient Greek version of the book is about one-eighth shorter and arranges some chapters differently.
intro.purpose: To call Judah back to its covenant with God, to announce the judgment that came through Babylon, and to promise restoration and a new covenant written on the heart.
intro.bigIdea: God judges a people who break His covenant, but He will plant them again and write His law on their hearts.
